hints.text: An improper fraction counts everything in pieces of one size. How many thirds are inside each whole?
Each whole is $3$ thirds, so $4$ wholes are $4 \times 3 = 12$ thirds. Add the $2$ extra thirds from the fraction part.
$12 + 2 = 14$ thirds in all, so the improper fraction is $4\frac{2}{3} = \frac{14}{3}$.

explanation: One whole equals $\frac{3}{3}$, so four wholes equal $4 \times 3 = 12$ thirds.
The mixed number also has $\frac{2}{3}$ on top of the four wholes.
Altogether there are $12 + 2 = 14$ thirds, so the improper fraction is $\frac{14}{3}$.
Check by dividing: $14 \div 3 = 4$ remainder $2$, which is $4\frac{2}{3}$ again.

alternativeExplanations.title: The shortcut, and why it works
steps: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, then add the numerator: $4 \times 3 + 2 = 14$.
That is exactly the counting-thirds argument, done in one line ✓
